label: WARRANTED_CORRECTION_STANDARD_2: A standard an agent can actually use with adequate epistemic…
definition: A standard an agent can actually use with adequate epistemic warrant to distinguish correct from incorrect applications of a rule. Its practical availability and warrant are additional requirements beyond the extensional existence of a predicate on evidence.
note: Comparison sense only: no complete theory of epistemic warrant is asserted or formalized. Whether PI I.258/I.265 requires this or a different grammatical notion remains an open source-interpretive question. Do not infer it from the exact-classifier theorem. Declaration-completion investigation 2026-11-09: the separate CertifiedCorrection.Procedure candidate exposes decision, certificate, Boolean checking, execution resources, scope coverage and semantic calibration. It is not this definition: neither an accepted certificate nor even factive calibration is by itself adequate philosophical warrant. Both original sense allowances remain. To complete this shared definition, supply a substantive account of epistemic entitlement to the procedure and its calibration, with applicability to actual inquirers; use the same declaration for both existing senses, without wrappers.
